name: B-living-garden
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE high-fidelity desktop WEBSITE SCREENSHOT, 1536x1024 landscape, straight-on, edge to edge without browser chrome, device frame or external annotations. This is SproutLab, an existing English photosynthesis learning app for 10-year-old children. Redesign its active lesson screen, specifically the 'Your turn' phase of 'Sprout's food-making secret'. It is a usable children's learning activity, never a SaaS landing page, marketing page, dashboard, or poster. All text and controls must be large, crisp, correctly spelled and highly legible. Body text approximate 18–22px at this resolution, buttons at least 48px high. One dominant working visual and one obvious next action, compact navigation, very little prose. Show a coherent visual system an engineer could implement with semantic HTML buttons and SVG drawings. The central educational diagram MUST show a whole rooted plant with soil, connected stem and leaves; BLUE water travels INSIDE roots and stem to the leaf, never floating water droplets in air. A labeled magnified leaf slice may show chloroplasts, never a fantasy room or machine in a leaf. Sunlight provides energy. CO₂ enters through a tiny leaf opening. Sprout and Beep can appear as small supporting cartoon characters, with leaves rooted and robot outside the plant. No extra rewards, scores, new quizzes or timers. Show stop 2 of 7, and compact progression labels 'Story', 'Watch', 'Your turn' with Your turn active. Provide a 'Picture notes' link. Sound is optional. Keep the whole core activity and controls inside the screenshot. Avoid the rejected visual formula: warm cream canvas, forest-green chunky rounded headline, green pill navigation, lavender/yellow card grid, long title/subtitle masthead. No giant slogan, feature cards, testimonials, sign-up, pricing, gradient blobs, glassmorphism, gratuitous stickers or decorative dashboard statistics.
DIRECTION B — LIVING GARDEN. Make the experiment itself a charming spacious illustrated world, with a small conventional app navigation and floating-on-the-scene but clearly labeled HTML controls. Palette: large SKY BLUE #A9DFF2 upper field, rich lapis ink #17364A, juicy apple-green plant, terracotta soil cross-section along lower third, restrained sunflower-yellow action. White caption areas. NO cream, NO forest-green headings, NO pastel card grid. Art style: sophisticated storybook gouache shapes translated into crisp layered vector-like illustration, restrained subtle handmade edges, expressive plants but not preschool baby styling. Side-on whole rooted plant at very large scale centered x720, branching stem clearly connected to the leaves, open sky framing it. Soil cross-section occupies y680–865 revealing a broad root system. Water appears as a thin luminous blue line IN the roots and stem, not decorative floating drops. An enlarged leaf cross-section sits as a circular magnified inset right x1180/y425, with a connecting thin leader from the real leaf, label 'Inside this leaf', and small clean green chloroplast shapes. Sun with cloud at upper left; no fairy buildings, furniture, pipes or gears. The main plant/leaf scene fills nearly all screen under 64px navy app bar. Header has white SproutLab small left, 'Map', 'Journal', '2 of 7', 'Sound off'. Top-left of scene has compact two-line heading 'A leaf has a secret.' and instruction 'Trace the water to find it.' no large marketing hero typography. Beneath this small heading three simple underlined phase links 'Story', 'Watch', 'Your turn' (selected). Primary button 'Trace the water' blue with white text sits lower-left beside visible roots and is connected by a small purposeful leader, not a hidden hotspot. Bottom white control shelf is only 115px tall: left small Sprout character and readable caption 'Water moves from roots to leaves.'; middle two conventional clearly labeled controls 'Let carbon dioxide in' button and 'Sunlight' slider at low setting; right 'Picture notes' link. The sunlight slider is not oversized illustration. Clear controls need not match natural objects. Composition must look completely different from a boxed lesson page: scene-first, generous sky, very little chrome, age-10 sense of discovery, quiet and playful. Keep all important labels off complicated art.
